Article Title: ‘Lucknow Express engine failed’: Akhilesh takes ‘Delhi handing over command’ dig at BJP pressers

Rajnath Singh targets Congress during presser

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Friday took a 'engine of the Lucknow Express has failed' swipe at the BJP amid defence minister Rajnath Singh’s press conference in Lucknow.In a post on X, Yadav wrote, “I hear there's a big press conference happening from the side of those in power. It seems like the engine of the 'Lucknow Express' has failed, which is why Delhi's engine has made an internal decision to hand over the command of Lucknow to someone else. "Calling the press conference a “show”, the Samajwadi Party chief alleged that the real objective was to portray the leadership in Lucknow as ineffective and remove it permanently.“This press conference is just for show; the real game is to prove Lucknow's engine is a junker and permanently remove it. Now who will protect the people of Lucknow?” he added.At the press conference in Lucknow, defence minister Rajnath Singh targeted the Congress, highlighting its prolonged absence from power in Uttar Pradesh and questioning Rahul Gandhi’s ability to win his parliamentary constituency without the Samajwadi Party’s support.“The Congress party has been out of power in Uttar Pradesh for 37 years. I would like to ask Rahul Gandhi: without the Samajwadi Party, do you even have the capability to win your own seat in Rae Bareli?” Singh said.Uttar Pradesh is scheduled to hold its next Assembly elections in 2027, with the BJP and opposition parties expected to intensify their political campaigns in the run-up to the polls.
Article Summary: Rajnath Singh targets Congress during presser in Lucknow. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav calls press conference a'show' Uttar Pradesh is scheduled to hold its next Assembly elections in 2027. The BJP and opposition parties are expected to intensify their political campaigns.

Article Title: Ladakh talks inconclusive, next meet on October 22
Article Text:
The last such meeting was held on Sept 9 in New Delhi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: A crucial meeting on autonomy between a ministry of home affairs (MHA) subcommittee and Ladakhi representatives in Leh on Wednesday ended inconclusively, with both sides agreeing to hold talks again on Oct 22 in New Delhi.“The MHA team gave a presentation of its draft proposal and we submitted our draft. We found considerable gaps between the two. However, we have stressed that further discussions should take place soon,” Chering Dorjay Lakrook, co-chairman of Leh Apex Body (LAB), said Thursday.LAB member Sonam Wangchuk, who also attended the meeting, said the MHA would share a revised draft proposal with Ladakhi leaders on Friday morning as there was a huge gap between the drafts.“We will not say the meeting was a failure. It is a continuation process but it was not satisfactory. We are waiting for the revised draft and hope it will reflect some changes. The difference between the two proposals was like the difference between earth and sky. Instead of moving forward from the previous meeting, we have moved backwards,” Wangchuk said.Lakrook pointed out that LAB remained firm on its key demands including safeguards under Article 371 and a Union territory with a legislature.The last such meeting was held on Sept 9 in New Delhi. LAB and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA), the two Ladakh organisations negotiating with the Centre on autnomy, were part of the talks. Ladakh chief secretary of Ladakh Ashish Kundra had then spoken of “a sui generis model under Article 371 which does not exist anywhere in the country”.Ladakhi representatives have been in talks with the Centre since 2023 but the process stalled briefly after four people were killed and over 80 injured in alleged police firing on protesters demanding statehood in Leh in Sept last year.Earlier on Thursday, LAB condemned Beijing’s remarks on Ladakh, saying the region has never been part of China in recorded history but an integral part of India.
Article Summary: A crucial meeting on autonomy between a ministry of home affairs (MHA) subcommittee and Ladakhi representatives in Leh on Wednesday ended inconclusively. Both sides agreed to hold talks again on Oct 22 in New Delhi. LAB remained firm on its key demands including safeguards under Article 371 and a Union territory with a legislature.

Article Title: Can’t browbeat us, says Supreme Court, seeks replies from CEC, ECs on opposition plea
Article Text:
“No one can browbeat us. These are all fragile attempts. Nobody took notice of this,” the CJI said.

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday sought responses from EC, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on a petition filed by INDIA bloc functionaries led by Rahul Gandhi alleging irregularities in SIR, arbitrary deletion of voters, undemocratic functioning of the poll panel and flaws in EVM use, even as it slammed the suggestion that the court could be browbeaten by deploying crowds.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said it was issuing notices on the petition and would await the responses. It also issued notices on all petitions questioning the SIR process in different states but clarified that it would take them up state-wise instead of bunching them together.At this juncture, senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia said a petition had been filed along with a memorandum signed by 200-odd lawyers against Rahul for bringing his supporters in large numbers onto the SC premises on Oct 12 to file the petition in an attempt to browbeat the judiciary.CJI Kant took exception to the suggestion that it could be intimidated by mobilising crowds. “No one can browbeat us. These are all fragile attempts. Nobody took notice of this,” he said.He went on to take note of comments by senior lawyers who spoke about losing trust in the judiciary only to praise the institution immediately afterwards. “We know they say something outside and something else inside the court. We are not sitting in ivory towers.We are also aware of such things,” CJI Kant said.Recently, senior advocate Kapil Sibal had expressed disillusionment with SC but gave a statement about the court regaining people’s faith the very next day after it passed a particular order.The hearing started on an intriguing note when senior advocate Abhishek Manu Singhvi began arguments for Rahul and other netas on alleged irregularities in EC’s collective decision-making, and was interrupted by Sibal.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant took exception to the suggestion that it could be intimidated by mobilising crowds. “No one can browbeat us. These are all fragile attempts. Nobody took notice of this,” the CJI said.

Article Title: Special summary revision of poll roll in 17 states
Article Text:
Only for voter list updation; paused post-2024

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Election Commission Thursday ordered special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in 17 states/Union territories (UT) — including the five states due for assembly elections early next year — with reference to Jan 1, 2027 as the qualifying date.This is the first SSR exercise — which, unlike special intensive revision (SIR) that prepares electoral roll de novo, is a mere updation of the roll with no house-to-house visits by booth-level officers (BLOs) — to be undertaken after it was paused post-2024, on account of SIR that started with Bihar in June 2025 and has since covered 31 states/UTs in back-to-back phases. The third phase of SIR, covering 19 states/UTs, is still underway, with only a few states completed.As per the SSR schedule announced for 17 states/UTs — Assam, Andaman & Nicobar, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Goa, Gujarat, Kerala, Lakshadweep, MP, Manipur, Puducherry, Punjab, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, UP, Uttarakhand and West Bengal — rationalisation of polling stations will be completed by Nov 2.Draft rolls shall be published on Nov 12, followed by the claims and objections window from Nov 12 to Dec 11 and their disposal by Dec 28.Final rolls for the 17 states/UTs will be published on Jan 4, 2027.EC added that the schedule for the 19 states/UTs covered in Phase 3 as well as Himachal, J&K and Ladakh, where SIR has not yet been ordered, shall be announced later.The non-conduct of SSR after Jan 2024, barring Assam where it was completed ahead of polls earlier this year, was purportedly one of the points of alleged disagreements between ECs S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, on the one hand, and CEC Gyanesh Kumar, on the other.
Article Summary: EC orders special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in 17 states/Union territories. This is the first SSR exercise to be undertaken after it was paused post-2024. The third phase of SIR covering 19 states/UTs is still underway, with only a few states completed.

Article Title: Government invokes ‘catastrophic event’ clause against 3 highway developers
Article Text:
TOI has learnt that the road transport ministry recently notified a “catastrophic event” in the case of widening and strengthening of a 45-km stretch of NH-727B in Uttar Pradesh after an accident during construction claimed two lives and left one with grievous injury in March.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a first, the road transport ministry has invoked the newly introduced provision on “catastrophic” failure against three highway developers, signalling a tougher crackdown on contractors and concessionaires responsible for poor construction quality and major structural failures on National Highway projects.The provision of “catastrophic event” allows highway owning agencies to bar the highway developers for two years from bidding for new projects. Such highway builders also face negative ratings that will adversely impact their chances of getting future projects.TOI has learnt that the road transport ministry recently notified a “catastrophic event” in the case of widening and strengthening of a 45-km stretch of NH-727B in Uttar Pradesh after an accident during construction claimed two lives and left one with grievous injury in March. The joint venture of VRC Constructions and R&C Infra Engineers has challenged this in the Delhi High Court, and the matter is pending before it.In the second case, the ministry has notified this penal provision in the contract following a 2-meter settlement of pavement, failure of reinforced earth wall foundation, displacement and tilting of wall blocks and cracking of adjoining ground of a portion of the Poondiyankuppam-Sattanathapuram section of NH-45A in Tamil Nadu.The concessionaire Poondiyankuppam-Sattanathapuram Section Pvt Ltd (of Oriental) has reportedly moved the court as well.In the third case, a show cause notice for “catastrophic event” has been issued to JV of Wagad Infra Project and Sorathia Velji Ratna for collapse of a reinforced earth wall at Shahpura on Jabalpur-Hiran river section of NH-12 in Madhya Pradesh.A catastrophic event in a highway project refers to major failures such as the collapse of bridges, flyovers or tunnels; severe pavement or embankment damage forcing traffic closure; concrete pavement failure beyond prescribed limits; or construction equipment collapse resulting in loss of life. Under the new framework, such failures can attract penalties in the performance ratings of contractors and concessionaires.
Article Summary: The provision of “catastrophic event’ allows highway owning agencies to bar the highway developers for two years from bidding for new projects. The joint venture of VRC Constructions and R&C Infra Engineers has challenged this in the Delhi High Court, and the matter is pending before it.

Article Title: Is Dhanush ready to make his political debut? Fan club's new avatar sparks buzz
Article Text:
Actor Dhanush’s organisation has unveiled a new flag and logo and plans to establish a grassroots network across five assembly constituencies in Coimbatore.

From MGR to Vijay: The stars in politics

What has Dhanush said

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Actor Dhanush 's official fan club has been restructured as the 'Dhanush Narpani Iyakkam' (Dhanush Welfare Movement), fuelling speculation about a possible political debut. The organisation unveiled a new flag and logo and announced plans to build a local network across five assembly constituencies in Coimbatore district.The restructuring was approved at an executive meeting in Coimbatore on Wednesday, news agency PTI reported. The new red-and-white flag features a large red star, with Dhanush's image at the centre.The move has drawn comparisons with actor Vijay , whose fan network evolved into a grassroots organisation before he launched the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK). TVK went on to emerge as the single-largest party in the 2026 Tamil Nadu assembly elections, winning 108 of 234 seats and forming the government with allies.Dhanush, however, has not announced any plans to enter politics.The emphasis on constituency-level organisation is a key aspect of the restructuring. The movement plans to establish local welfare units and enroll members across five assembly constituencies in Coimbatore district.Such networks can help coordinate community activities and build a sustained local presence. However, there is no confirmation that the organisation is preparing for electoral campaigning.Coimbatore could be a significant testing ground for a new political force. In the 2026 assembly elections, TVK won six of the district's 10 seats.Tamil Nadu has a long history of film stars translating screen popularity into political influence. MG Ramachandran, popularly known as MGR, founded the AIADMK in 1972 after his association with the DMK and became chief minister in 1977. His popularity helped build a political movement, backed by an organisational network and a distinct political identity.J Jayalalithaa, who followed a similar path from cinema to politics, also went on to become chief minister.Vijay is the latest major example. He made a strong electoral debut by clinching the CM chair in the first attempt itself.The latest restructuring follows Dhanush's appeal to supporters to move beyond film celebrations and focus on community welfare.At a blood donation camp organised by his fan clubs in Chennai in July, the actor had urged them to use their collective strength to understand local needs and help families facing difficulties.Reports have also circulated about a possible political outfit named Tamilaga Ezhuchi Kazhagam, but formal registration with the Election Commission has not been confirmed.In September, when asked about a possible political debut after receiving his National Film Awards, Dhanush laughed off the question.So, is a political debut on the cards?The new name, flag, logo and plans for local welfare units give Dhanush's fan association a more structured identity. But these steps do not, by themselves, establish that he is preparing to contest elections.A formal political announcement, a declared agenda or confirmation of party formation would provide clearer indications of his intentions. None has emerged so far.For now, the Dhanush Narpani Iyakkam could remain a welfare organisation or evolve into something larger. The political speculation is growing, but the actor has yet to signal that he is ready to make the leap from cinema to electoral politics.
Article Summary: Actor Dhanush's fan club has been restructured as the 'Dhanush Narpani Iyakkam' The organisation unveiled a new flag and logo and announced plans to build a local network across five assembly constituencies in Coimbatore district. Move has drawn comparisons with actor Vijay, whose fan network evolved into a grassroots organisation.

Article Title: ‘Anything possible in politics’: Sachin Pilot on speculation over Amarinder Singh’s return to Congress
Article Text:
Sachin Pilot keeps door open on Amarinder Singh’s Congress return

Amarinder Singh’s discontent with BJP

Singh’s journey from Congress to BJP

Pilot to undertake five-day Punjab yatra

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sachin Pilot has said “anything is possible in politics” when asked about speculation that former Punjab chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh could return to the Congress, while stressing that he has not spoken to Singh about his political plans.In an exclusive interview with news agency PTI, Pilot, the Congress’ in-charge of Punjab, described Singh as someone who had served the state “well” and was “a man of a very tall stature”.However, he said he had not discussed with the former chief minister the possibility of joining or leaving any political party.“As far as Captain sahab is concerned, I've known him personally since I was very young. And I've worked closely with him. Personally, I've not had any interaction with him on this particular issue. But like they say, politics mein 'kuch bhi ho sakta hai' (Anything is possible in politics)?” Pilot said.“I mean, who knows? I think he's actually, just like me, part of the armed forces. He's served Punjab well. And he's a man of a very tall stature, certainly. How the BJP has taken to him, I'm not sure,” he added.Pilot said he had seen Singh's recent critical remarks about the BJP but had not spoken to him personally about his future plans.Asked whether Singh might expect a prominent position if he returned to the Congress, Pilot said he could not comment on what the former chief minister was thinking.“I don't know what he's (Captain) thinking. I've not spoken to him or had any communication on that front. Time will tell what happens. I can't say anything right now,” Pilot said.The speculation about Singh's possible return to the Congress has gathered attention amid his recent expressions of dissatisfaction with the BJP. Last month, Singh said the party had not consulted him on Punjab. He maintained that it was his duty to convey his views on the state to the BJP and that doing so did not mean he was quitting the party.Singh also said he was going through “difficult times” but did not elaborate.Speculation about his political future had begun in August, when Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha, named Singh as his favourite politician from the BJP during an ‘Ask me’ session on Instagram.Responding to Rahul's remarks, Singh said his personal relationship with the Gandhi family would always remain but his political commitment was to the BJP.Singh was among the Congress’ prominent regional leaders in Punjab and led the party to a landslide victory in the 117-member state Assembly in 2017, becoming chief minister for a second time.He served as chief minister from 2002 to 2007 and again from 2017 to 2021. He resigned from the post and left the Congress in 2021 following infighting within the party's Punjab unit.Singh subsequently formed the Punjab Lok Congress (PLC), which failed to win any seats in the 2022 Punjab Assembly elections. The party was later merged with the BJP.His wife and former MP Preneet Kaur, son Raninder Singh and daughter Jai Inder Kaur are also with the BJP.Singh has served as a Punjab MLA, a Lok Sabha MP and president of the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee on three occasions.Separately, Pilot is scheduled to undertake a five-day yatra across Punjab from October 16 to 20 to meet families who have lost relatives to gangster violence and alleged failures in law and order.The Congress said the yatra would cover Moga, Bathinda, Mansa, Ludhiana, Jalandhar, Kapurthala, Hoshiarpur, Pathankot, Gurdaspur, Tarn Taran and Amritsar.During the visits, Pilot will meet bereaved families, offer condolences and hear their accounts of the crimes and the responses they have received from the police and the state government, the party said.The Congress said several families had waited months, and in some cases years, for arrests, chargesheets or a fair trial in cases involving killings claimed by or linked to organised gangs.The party said the yatra aimed to bring the families' demands for justice to the public and the state government and, where necessary, to the courts.It also said Pilot would highlight what it described as a deterioration in law and order under the Aam Aadmi Party government in Punjab.
Article Summary: Congress leader Sachin Pilot says 'anything is possible in politics' Pilot says he has not spoken to Captain Amarinder Singh about his political plans. Pilot is scheduled to undertake a five-day yatra across Punjab from October 16 to 20.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan (PTI Photo)

-

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: “I felt it was extremely important to give back”: How Justin Herbert’s $25,000 donation helped provide 100,000 meals to families in Los Angeles
Article Text:
Justin Herbert’s $25,000 donation helped provide 100,000 meals to families in Los Angeles(Getty Images)

Justin Herbert's $25,000 donation helped put 100,000 meals on the table

Why the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank needed support during the holidays

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert has given fans plenty to cheer about on the football field. But in Dec. 2021, he made headlines for something beyond football. Herbert donated $25,000 to the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank, helping provide 100,000 meals to children and families across Los Angeles County. The donation arrived just before the holidays, when many families were struggling to put food on the table.The gesture was also very personal for the QB He credited his parents for teaching him to help others and said he wanted to support the community he called home. At a time when many people were still dealing with the effects of the pandemic, the Chargers quarterback wanted to do his part.On Dec. 15, 2021, the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank announced Herbert's $25,000 contribution. The donation was enough to help distribute 100,000 meals throughout Los Angeles County during the holiday season.The need remained high even as life began returning to normal for some people. Families across the county continued to face food insecurity, with many still feeling the financial effects of the COVID-19 pandemic. The Food Bank reported that it was distributing more than twice as much food as it had before the pandemic.Herbert wanted to help his neighbours through that difficult period. In a statement released by the organisation, he explained what had inspired him to make the donation."My parents always instilled in my brothers and me the importance of service to others," Herbert said. "As a member of this community, I felt it was extremely important to give back and support my neighbors. People are in need, and it's our job to come together and help."His words reflected the values his family had taught him. Rather than treating charitable work as something separate from his life as an NFL player, Herbert saw it as a responsibility to the people around him.The contribution also built on the Los Angeles Chargers' earlier support for the same organisation. During the pandemic, the team had made a significant donation to help people affected by layoffs and reduced working hours.The Los Angeles Regional Food Bank had been working to fight hunger in the county since 1973. Its network of 700 partner agencies helped distribute food and groceries to people who needed assistance, including children and families facing financial hardship.At the time of Herbert's donation, the organisation was providing food assistance to an average of 900,000 people every month. It also relied on donations and the efforts of around 15,000 volunteers to keep its programmes running.The Food Bank's donation model helped make contributions go further. According to the organisation, every dollar donated could provide four meals to someone facing food insecurity. Herbert's $25,000 gift therefore offered meaningful support during a particularly difficult time of year.Michael Flood, the organisation's president and CEO, expressed his gratitude for the quarterback's contribution. He noted that although the numbers had fallen from their pandemic peak, the Food Bank was still distributing more than twice the amount of food it had handled before the outbreak.Flood's comments highlighted the ongoing challenge facing families across Los Angeles County. The holiday season can bring additional pressure for households already struggling with everyday expenses, making community support especially valuable.Herbert's donation helped the organisation continue its work when many families needed assistance. It also showed how an individual contribution, backed by a local charity's distribution network, could reach people across a large community.In Justin’s case, the gesture came down to a simple belief: people should help one another when they can. His $25,000 contribution did more than fund meals. It helped the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank continue supporting children and families during a difficult holiday season.
Article Summary: Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert donated $25,000 to the Los Angeles Regional Food Bank. The donation helped provide 100,000 meals to children and families across Los Angeles County. Herbert said he wanted to help his neighbours through that difficult period.

Article Title: Who was Yoo Ji-won? 25-year-old runner dies after collapsing near Seoul Race finish line
Article Text:
Who was Yoo Ji-won? 25-year-old runner dies after collapsing near Seoul Race finish line

Yoo Ji-won was a KAIST researcher who shared her running journey online

Yoo Ji-won collapsed at 20.6km as Seoul Race organisers confirm death

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

South Korean running influencer Yoo Ji-won, 25, died after collapsing just 500 metres from the finish line of the Seoul Race half-marathon on October 11, 2026. She was rushed to a medical facility after the incident but could not be saved, according to the race organisers. Ji-won was also an artificial intelligence semiconductor researcher at the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST). She had built a following of more than 8,000 people on Instagram by sharing her running journey and race results. The cause of her death has not been publicly confirmed.Yoo Ji-won balanced her work in science with her passion for running. She researched artificial intelligence semiconductors at KAIST while sharing her training sessions and race performances with her Instagram followers.Her account, under the handle @mta1n_0ne, had attracted more than 8,000 followers. She regularly posted about her runs, giving people a look at her progress and achievements in the sport.Her final Instagram post, shared on October 4, showed her timing from a 10-kilometre run. Following news of her death, the post became a place for friends and followers to share their condolences and remember her.According to South Korean media reports, Ji-won had also achieved strong results in local races.She won the women’s masters 10-kilometre category at the Gunsan Saemangeum Marathon in April 2026. She had also completed the full Seoul Marathon in March, finishing in two hours, 56 minutes and 32 seconds, according to the International Business Times UK.The incident happened at around 8:49 am on October 11 during the 2026 Seoul Race half-marathon. Ji-won collapsed at the 20.6-kilometre mark, with roughly 500 metres left before the finish line of the 21.1-kilometre race.The Seoul Race Organizing Committee confirmed the death in a statement shared on Instagram. It said emergency first aid was provided at the scene before an ambulance took the participant to a medical facility for treatment.The committee’s statement read: “Around 8:49 AM on October 11, an emergency situation occurred when a participant in the Seoul Race Half Course collapsed at the 20.6km mark. After providing emergency first aid at the scene, the individual was transported to a medical facility via a 119 ambulance for treatment; however, sadly, the participant passed away.“We offer our deepest condolences to the bereaved family facing this sudden tragedy and pray for the repose of the soul of the deceased. We also extend our sympathies to the participants, whose hearts must be heavy upon hearing this tragic news. The Organizing Committee will closely examine the matter and take necessary follow-up measures,”The organisers said they would review what happened and take the necessary follow-up measures. However, they did not announce a cause of death. No official medical explanation for Ji-won’s collapse has been made public.The news also prompted an emotional tribute from her friend and fellow content creator Bummy, who described seeing a crowd near the finish line before learning what had happened.“Near the finish line of the Seoul Race, I saw a crowd gathering and thought someone must have been hurt. As soon as I crossed the finish line, I looked for you on the awards podium, but then came the unsettling news, and I began to sense a reality I didn’t want to believe,” Bummy wrote.His account reflected the shock of learning that a fellow runner had died during an event where participants had gathered to complete their races. For Ji-won’s friends and followers, her final running post has become a place to remember her achievements and share messages of support for her family.
Article Summary: Yoo Ji-won, 25, collapsed at the 20.6km mark of the 2026 Seoul Race half- marathon. She was rushed to a medical facility but could not be saved. The cause of her death has not been publicly confirmed. She had built a following of more than 8,000 people on Instagram.

Article Title: Naomi Osaka’s daughter Shai is already swinging a mini tennis racquet: How motherhood is changing the four-time Grand Slam champion’s perspective on life and tennis
Article Text:

How motherhood has changed Naomi Osaka’s tennis priorities

Naomi Osaka puts daughter Shai before tennis

Naomi Osaka sees tennis as more than winning

Naomi Osaka’s life as a four-time Grand Slam champion continues to evolve, but her most important role increasingly lies away from the tennis court,and the Japanese star has spoken openly about how becoming a mother changed her priorities, giving her a different perspective on victories, defeats and the demands of professional competition. Her daughter, Shai, is now a central part of that outlook.Ahead of the 2026 US Open, Osaka offered a glimpse into family life, revealing that her three-year-old daughter enjoys swinging a miniature tennis racquet at home, while Shai has not yet started playing on a proper tennis court, the small detail highlights how the sport is already present in the family’s everyday life. For Osaka, however, motherhood is not about preparing her daughter to follow in her footsteps. It has also helped her appreciate the value of life beyond tennis.For much of her career, Osaka’s identity was closely associated with her achievements on the court. She won the US Open in 2018 and 2020 and took two Australian Open titles to become one of the leading players of her generation, and her success brought global recognition, but it also came with the pressures of competing at the highest level.Motherhood has given Osaka another perspective on those expectations.Speaking before the 2026 US Open, she explained that people sometimes overlook her role as a parent because of her sporting profile. She described tennis as something of a “side hustle,” adding that her main job is being a mother. The remark reflected a change in priorities rather than a loss of interest in competition.Osaka’s comments suggest that tennis no longer defines every part of her identity. She continues to train and compete. But her life also revolves around spending time with Shai and making decisions that work for their family. That distinction can be significant for a touring athlete whose career involves travel, demanding schedules and time away from home.Her approach also reflects a more measured relationship with professional results. Titles and rankings remain part of elite tennis. But they are no longer the only measures of personal fulfillment. Osaka has discussed how becoming a mother changed the way she views her career and life. Also, describing a greater sense of happiness as she balances both responsibilities.Shai was born in July 2023, during Osaka’s break from professional tennis for pregnancy and childbirth. The arrival of her daughter marked a major personal transition for the former world No. 1, who returned to competition in 2024. Since then, Osaka has continued navigating the challenge of combining motherhood with the international tennis calendar.Osaka’s recent comments make clear that parenting is not simply another responsibility alongside tennis. It has become a central part of how she evaluates her time and career. Her decision to skip the Cincinnati tournament ahead of the 2026 US Open, as reported by the tournament’s official website, was connected to wanting to spend time at home with her daughter. She subsequently said she felt ready to return for the New York major.The balance is not necessarily straightforward. Professional tennis requires athletes to maintain their fitness, prepare for opponents and travel frequently, and parenting a young child creates different needs and routines, meaning tournament choices can involve considerations beyond rankings or competitive momentum.Osaka has spoken candidly about her mental health struggles and the pressures she has faced during her career, and her experiences have helped shine a light on conversations about athlete wellbeing. Having children has expanded her identity, but it would be naïve to suggest parenthood is a cure-all for mental health problems. Instead, her comments indicate that family life has become an important source of perspective as she continues competing.For Osaka, being Shai’s mother and being a professional tennis player can coexist. The difference is that success on the court no longer has to define her entire sense of self. Her daughter gives her another role to value, including on days when tennis does not go as planned.Shai’s interest in swinging a mini racquet has introduced a playful connection between Osaka’s professional world and her family life. The toddler has not yet taken to a real court, according to Osaka’s comments ahead of the US Open. The champion has not suggested that her daughter must become a tennis player, leaving the possibility of a future sporting interest open without setting expectations.Osaka has emphasized that sports can help children develop qualities that extend beyond competition. She has pointed to discipline and other personal characteristics she believes she gained through tennis, and those lessons can matter whether a child eventually pursues professional sport or simply enjoys physical activity as part of growing up.That outlook marks a different emphasis from the intense demands of the professional circuit. At the elite level, results are measured through titles, rankings and match statistics, and for a young child, however, playing with a small racquet can simply be a way to explore, imitate a parent and have fun.Osaka’s own relationship with tennis has also continued to evolve since her return. Rather than presenting motherhood as a reason to abandon her ambitions, she has described a life in which competition and parenting sit alongside one another, with family increasingly influencing her choices.As she continues her career, Shai’s miniature racquet offers a small but telling glimpse of that new perspective. Osaka remains a major figure in women’s tennis, but she is also a parent who wants to protect time with her daughter and appreciate the lessons sport can offer outside the pursuit of trophies. Whether Shai eventually chooses tennis for herself remains to be seen. For now, Osaka’s priority is allowing that interest to develop naturally while embracing her own life as both a champion and a mother.
Article Summary: Naomi Osaka has spoken openly about how becoming a mother changed her priorities. The four-time Grand Slam champion said her main job is being a mother. Her three-year-old daughter, Shai, enjoys swinging a miniature tennis racquet.

Article Title: "It's not fair": Tom Brady made heartbreaking admission about his children facing unfair struggles because of their famous parents

Tom Brady balances co-parenting and family time after divorce

In 2023, Tom Brady opened up about a side of fame that rarely gets the same attention as his Super Bowl victories and record-breaking NFL career. The former quarterback admitted that growing up with famous parents can put pressure on children who never asked for the spotlight. As a father of three, Brady said he wanted his children to have the freedom to develop their own identities instead of living up to public expectations. His comments offered a personal look at the challenges of raising a family while navigating worldwide attention and the demands of celebrity life.During an interview with TODAY.com published in June 2023, Brady discussed how his celebrity status could affect his children's childhoods. He shares two children, Benjamin and Vivian, with his former wife, Gisele Bündchen, and has an older son, Jack, with former girlfriend Bridget Moynahan.Brady explained that his children face expectations he did not experience while growing up. Their parents' success can lead people to make assumptions about their abilities, appearance and future, even before they have a chance to discover their own interests."Our children have unique challenges [that are] different from ones I had growing up," Brady told the outlet. "There are a lot of expectations because of who their mom or their dad is, and it's not necessarily fair to them because they didn't choose that."The seven-time Super Bowl champion also stressed that his children should not have to match public expectations simply because of their family background.His message was straightforward. Being the child of a sports icon or an internationally recognised model does not mean someone will automatically share their parents' talents or ambitions.His own experience as an elite athlete may have given him a greater appreciation for the pressure that comes with public attention. However, Brady made it clear that his children deserve room to grow as individuals.His comments also highlighted a challenge many celebrity families face: protecting their children's privacy and individuality when public curiosity follows them from an early age.Brady's remarks came during his first summer of co-parenting with Bündchen following their divorce, which was finalised in October 2022 after 13 years of marriage.Despite the family changes, the former couple had plans to give their children a memorable summer. Brady told People that he was organising their schedule and looking forward to spending time with them."I've got my little calendar right here," Brady said.The plans included a family trip to Disneyland, followed by travel to Brazil with Bündchen and a European trip with Brady."They got lots of good plans," he said. "These kids have a really good summer lined up."Brady also spoke warmly about watching Jack play football, describing the experience as enjoyable. His enthusiasm showed that, despite his demanding career, he valued the chance to support his son's interests.Ultimately, Brady's comments offered a reminder that family life brings challenges even for people who appear to have it all. For him, helping his children build confidence and find their own paths matters just as much as his achievements on the football field.
Article Summary: Tom Brady opens up about his children's struggles with fame. The former quarterback admitted that growing up with famous parents can put pressure on children who never asked for the spotlight. Brady said he wanted his children to have the freedom to develop their own identities instead of living up to public expectations.

How Tom Brady’s golf experience raised $120,000 for Best Buddies

Why Best Buddies has remained close to Tom Brady

Tom Brady has spent years supporting Best Buddies International, a nonprofit that works with people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. On Nov.17, 2023, the former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback helped the organisation raise money through a golf experience that fetched $120,000 at its Miami gala.The auction offered more than a chance to play golf with an NFL legend. It supported a cause Brady had backed for over two decades, with the event raising $5 million in total for Best Buddies programs.At the 25th Annual Best Buddies Miami Gala, Brady co-hosted a live auction with Anthony K. Shriver, the organisation’s founder, chairman and CEO. Their auction featured a golf experience and lunch at Indian Creek Golf Course. The package raised $120,000 for the nonprofit.Best Buddies announced the results on Nov. 22, 2023, in its official event report. The gala took place five days earlier and also honoured Brady with the Spirit of Leadership Award for his contributions to the organisation.The evening included a dinner, live and silent auctions, and a performance by Grammy-winning artist Nelly. Brady also tossed autographed footballs into the crowd as part of the fundraising effort.The golf auction formed one part of a larger event. Best Buddies said the gala raised $5 million to support its work creating opportunities for friendship, employment, leadership development and inclusive living for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.Brady’s involvement with Best Buddies goes well beyond one fundraising night. The organisation said he had served as a global ambassador, advocate and supporter for more than 20 years by November 2023. His work helped the nonprofit raise over $100 million.During his acceptance speech at the November 17, 2023, Miami gala, Brady spoke about the value of relationships and support systems.“There is nothing in our life that can be accomplished as an individual,” Brady said at the event. “It always comes down to who’s in our life, who’s supporting us and who our friends are. That’s what the Best Buddies mission is all about.”Best Buddies works to build friendships and create opportunities for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Its programs also support employment, leadership and independent living.Brady’s support for Best Buddies also reflects his belief in the role that friendship and strong personal connections play in people’s lives. His remarks at the gala went beyond the auction itself, highlighting the value of having people who offer support and encouragement. That message aligns with the organisation’s work to help people with intellectual and developmental disabilities build meaningful relationships and find greater opportunities in their communities.The gala showed how Brady used his public profile to help raise funds for that mission. The $120,000 golf experience was one part of the effort while the event’s $5 million total supported Best Buddies programs on a wider scale.

Article Title: ‘I got it late, but I got it’: Told she was too old, Suchika Tariyal went from judo, kurash and ju-jitsu to Asian Games MMA bronze
Article Text:
Suchika Tariyal

Suchika Tariyal

The girl who wanted to learn how to fight

Another sport, another beginning

Suchika

Suchika MMA

When they stopped asking for help

Suchika with her husband Kapil

The 700 grams

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Suchika first Indian athlete to win an Asian Games medal in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA)

The gym where Suchika Tariyal trains is modest: a single floor, a makeshift mat, a cage and the equipment needed to prepare for mixed martial arts. It is owned by Vikas Dahiya, an MMA fighter himself. When Dahiya is out of town, the keys are with Tariyal and her husband, Kapil Hooda.The couple have become so invested in the place that it is more than a training facility. It is part of the routine around which they have organised their lives, with Kapil closely watching his wife's preparation and sharing the emotional highs and lows of her career.For years, that routine was built around a goal that kept slipping out of reach. Tariyal moved from one combat sport to another, dealt with selection hurdles, and came close to walking away more than once. The medal she had chased since childhood finally arrived at 36, when she became India's first Asian Games medallist in MMA.“For me, it's more than my life. Because I had a dream since childhood, which has come true today. I mean, I got it late, but I got it. I am very happy about it. I can't believe I have achieved it.I still can't believe it. But I feel like I have to do more. That's what's in my mind.”The bronze was a first for Indian MMA. Tariyal, though, was still thinking about the final she had missed. The semifinal against Singapore’s Hui Hoon Teo went to an additional round and was decided by a weigh-in tiebreak. Tariyal was 700 grams heavier and missed the final.“But I missed a gold medal. I was very sad. I had planned to win gold. But it did not happen. I am very sad about it.”The disappointment was familiar. Her sporting career had been marked by moments when she came close to a breakthrough, only for circumstances to push her towards another route. Judo had been her first sport, followed by kurash and ju-jitsu, before MMA gave her another chance at an Asian Games medal.The medal also carried the memory of a time when she had considered walking away altogether.“I had a desire from my childhood, which I made my life and I didn't achieve - either Commonwealth or Asian Games or Olympics. I wanted to get a medal. I wanted people to know about my struggling life, or how I reached here, or how my family helped me reach here.”Tariyal grew up in Chhawla, near Najafgarh in Delhi, one of four sisters. Her introduction to combat sports came not from a dream of winning medals or building an international career, but from an experience that left her feeling vulnerable as a child.When she was around 12 and sporting a ‘boy cut’, a barber at a salon touched her inappropriately. She returned home without telling her family what had happened, frightened and unsure how to process the incident. The experience stayed with her and eventually shaped her decision to learn how to fight back.“The barber touched me wrongly. I felt very bad. I did not know what was going on. I did not know why this happened to me.”“I did not tell anyone. I did not tell my family. I did not want to go out. I did not want to play. I did not know what to do. I wanted to learn a fighting game, so that if this happens again, I can do it.”Her mother eventually enrolled her in judo. Tariyal had wanted to learn boxing, but she took to judo quickly.“I was crazy about it. I didn't want to study or do anything. I just wanted to play judo. I wanted to give my 100% in judo.”She became an eight-time national judo champion. She won silver at the 2018 Commonwealth Judo Championships, gold at the 2019 edition and gold at the 2019 South Asian Games.Tariyal spent 15 years in judo and tried to qualify for the Olympics, but the Covid-19 pandemic disrupted that pursuit. At the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, she lost the bronze-medal bout in the final seconds.The route to the Asian Games through judo had also become difficult. Ranking requirements made selection challenging, so she turned to kurash, which offered another pathway.She trained for around a year and won the selection trials, but her name was not cleared for the 2023 Asian Games in Hangzhou until the final days before the competition.“Due to two federations, we were left behind. I didn’t have my name on the list. At that time, Mr Anurag Thakur was the sports minister. He helped us a lot. He made us understand. He listened to us. I got my name in the last moment, but I didn’t get enough training because we were running to get my name cleared.”She competed in kurash at Hangzhou but lost.After leaving kurash, Tariyal took up ju-jitsu and became a world champion in 2024. But the achievement did not guarantee a clear path forward, with the sport’s recognition in India remaining an obstacle. MMA offered another route, giving her a fresh opportunity to pursue the Asian Games medal she had long wanted.Pooja Tomar and Himanshu Kaushik encouraged her to try the sport. Tomar is a trailblazer in Indian MMA: she became the first Indian woman to compete in the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) in June 2024, and the first Indian fighter to win a bout in the promotion. Kaushik also guided Tariyal towards the sport.Tomar's presence is not limited to that early advice. She lives one floor above Tariyal and Kapil in their apartment complex on the outskirts of Gurugram. The proximity is part of the small circle around the fighter, a network of people who have encouraged her to continue when other routes have closed.Because of her judo background, she was comfortable with grappling but had to develop her striking. “I am a grappler. I have a judo background. It was difficult for me. I wanted to learn striking,” she said.She gradually worked on the new skills and that transition also opened a route into professional MMA. Tariyal signed a five-fight deal with BRAVE Combat Federation, making her promotional debut at BRAVE CF 92 in Bahrain in December 2024.The deal offered a way to continue competing professionally while she pursued the Asian Games pathway. Tariyal said she had completed two fights under the contract, with three remaining. Her judo background also shaped her choice of traditional MMA for the Asian Games, where the use of a gi (Judogi) and the emphasis on grappling and throws suited her strengths.Tariyal's career has involved repeated reinvention and each change required her to adapt her training and start again, often without the certainty that the new discipline would bring the medal she wanted. But the setbacks were not only about results or injuries. As she grew older, she began hearing a different kind of criticism: that she was too old to continue.Kapil, who works in Manesar, had seen how much Tariyal had given to sport. By the time they married, she had a job and a home, but years of chasing a major medal had left her close to giving up. Kapil urged her to continue, even as the financial burden of keeping her career going grew.“My husband had faith in me. I had given up. I was married and had a good job. I had a house and a husband. Then he believed in me, that I can do it. ‘I have seen you doing it,’” Tariyal said.Keeping her career going cost money. She took unpaid leave from work to train and compete, while overseas camps and travel had to be paid for without any guarantee of a result.“He spent from his pocket, took loans and he trained me. He sent me to Bali. I went there three-four times for two months. I have a job, and when I go for training, I go without pay. I don't get paid. Whatever I needed, he spent it.”Kapil approached people for financial help, but was repeatedly told that Tariyal was too old to continue. Eventually, he stopped asking and concentrated on doing what he could himself.Tariyal also looked for ways to find sponsors. During COVID-19, she appeared on reality television, hoping the exposure might help fund training and competition.“I thought if I do two-four events, I might get a sponsor,” she said. “If I get a sponsor, I will do it.”However, she dislocated her elbow during one of the shows. The injury put her preparation for the 2022 Commonwealth Games at risk. Even though she recovered in time to compete, she decided not to return to reality shows until she had achieved her sporting goals.“I decided I won't go to such reality shows until I achieve. I have to focus on my work,” she said.The doubts about her age continued. Tariyal said she heard at training camps that she should step aside and give younger athletes a chance.“A lot of people meet me and say that you have become so old. You have become 30 years old. You can’t play [the sport],” she said. “We still get to hear in the camps that you are too old. You shouldn't play now. You should drop now. You should give a chance to the youth ahead. So, I have heard this many times.”Her response was to keep competing. “As long as my body is working or I want to play, I can play. And you have seen that I have won a medal,” she said. “The more demotivating people I met in my life, the more motivated I got.”When she moved into MMA, Tariyal said, the federation - MMA-SFI (Mixed Martial Arts Sports Federation of India) - helped with training, food and other requirements and allowed her to use its gym without monthly fees.“I haven't seen such a federation,” she said.She credits Kapil with helping her stay in sport long enough to reach the Asian Games podium. “I would like to thank him. That's why I reached here. It was his dream, which I fulfilled.”At Aichi-Nagoya, the pressure of the opening bout was clear to Tariyal. She admitted to her coach that she was scared, only for him to tell her that he felt the same way, but believed she would do well.“I was very nervous at that time. I told my coach that I was scared. He said, ‘It's fair. You are scared, so you are telling the truth.’ I said, ‘Yes, I am scared.’ He said, ‘It's okay, I am scared too. But you will do well. I know you have worked very hard.’”She focused on winning the quarterfinal and securing a medal. “I had a belief that I have to win this round. Only then I will be able to secure a medal. I played all out. I don't know how I performed in the first round. I was very disturbed. Will my body work or not? What kind of performance will come? I played and I won. I was very happy.”The win assured her of bronze. The semifinal tiebreak kept her out of the final by 700 grams. At 36, Tariyal had finally won the Asian Games medal she had wanted since childhood.For now, Tariyal’s focus shifts to the World Championships in November. She will travel to Mumbai to prepare for the event, while the two remaining bouts on her BRAVE Combat Federation contract remain on the back burner.
Article Summary: Suchika Tariyal is the first Indian athlete to win an Asian Games medal in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA) The 36-year-old missed the final because she was 700 grams heavier. Her introduction to combat sports came not from a dream of winning medals, but from an experience that left her feeling vulnerable.

Article Title: Mumbai under heatwave warning for third consecutive day
Article Text:
IMD issued a heatwave warning for Thursday





MUMBAI: The city was under a heatwave warning for the third consecutive day on Wednesday with a yellow alert issued by the IMD For Oct 14, the weather bureau has warned of hot and humid weather conditions in isolated areas as temperatures continue to remain elevated.Maximum temperature recorded on Wednesday by the IMD Santacruz observatory was 37.8 deg C, which was 4.1 deg C above normal, while the IMD Colaba observatory recorded 36.4 deg C, which was 3.2 deg C above normal.Mumbai has been placed under a heatwave warning for Oct 15, with Oct 16 forecast to witness hot and humid weather conditions. Meanwhile, light to moderate rain and thundershowers are expected for Oct 17-18 for Mumbai and Thane.Just a day ago, the city had recorded a maximum temperature of 38°C, making it the second-hottest Oct day in 11 years. Meanwhile, mercury had touched 38.2°C on Monday, the highest Oct maximum recorded in the city during the same period.IMD officials too agreed that a prolonged heatwave for early in the month of Oct wasn’t very common.“The anticyclone which led to the first heatwave warning on Oct 9 last week has shifted slightly northwards, but an easterly wave is influencing the region, with temperatures likely to touch 37.8°C on Thursday.This will mean seven consecutive days of temperatures above 37°C, which is unusually oppressive for Mumbai. While the city does experience spells of two to three days of high temperatures, a continuous stretch of six to seven days is not normal. An easterly wave is a weather system characterised by a trough that travels from east to west. It is a feature of this season and can interact with weather systems approaching from the west, triggering intense thunderstorms. Its role in prolonging the current hot spell is a factor that needs to be examined, particularly in the context of a strong El Niño year,” said an IMD official.According to Akshay Sunil, Vice President, WeatherEx Pvt Ltd, “The heat over Mumbai is part of a broader warm spell across western India. A high-pressure circulation and easterly to northeasterly winds are limiting the usual cooling sea breeze, while clear post-monsoon skies are allowing strong daytime heating. Humidity adds to the discomfort. Our extended outlook suggests that above-normal temperatures may continue through at least October 22, although local light showers could bring temporary relief post Oct 22 in parts of Konkan. ”
Article Summary: Mumbai has been placed under a heatwave warning for Oct 15, with Oct 16 forecast to witness hot and humid weather conditions. Light to moderate rain and thundershowers are expected for Oct 17-18 for Mumbai and Thane. Maximum temperature recorded on Wednesday by the IMD Santacruz observatory was 37.8 deg C, 4.1 deg C above normal.

Article Title: Jaipur Murder: A poll contest, a family clash, 2 murders: How man killed his only son, daughter-in-law
Article Text:

Dispute over sarpanch election

Couple run over while returning home

Voting scheduled for November 16





JAIPUR: A 60-year-old man allegedly ran over his only son and daughter-in-law with an SUV in Rajasthan’s Churu district after a dispute over his decision to contest the upcoming panchayat elections , police said.The incident took place late Tuesday night in Changoi village, under Taranagar tehsil. The accused, identified as Ramchandra Jat, has been taken into custody, and an investigation is underway.Taranagar police station head constable Suresh Kumar said Ramchandra operates a weighbridge in the village and wanted to contest the sarpanch election from Changoi.His 40-year-old son, Ravindra, and 35-year-old daughter-in-law, Mahindra, were allegedly opposed to his decision. This had led to frequent clashes between them over the past few days, police said.Another argument broke out at their home on Tuesday night. Ramchandra and Ravindra subsequently went to the weighbridge, and Mahindra joined them there after some time. The dispute over contesting the election allegedly continued at the site.Police said Ravindra and Mahindra were returning home when Ramchandra allegedly approached them from behind in his Bolero jeep and hit them, running them over.Locals rushed to the spot after hearing screams and alerted the police. The couple was taken to a government hospital in Taranagar, where their bodies were placed in the mortuary.Ravindra ran an e-Mitra shop in the village, while Mahindra was a homemaker. The couple is survived by their 11-year-old daughter.The incident comes ahead of the panchayat elections in Taranagar, where voting for the posts of panch and sarpanch is scheduled for November 16 as part of the fourth phase of the ongoing elections.Changoi was recently declared a new gram panchayat. Ramchandra reportedly became determined to contest the sarpanch election after the change.Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident.

Article Title: #ByInvitation: ‘The Times of India pioneered the thought that art was money, and it can take credit for recognising that’
Article Text:
Writing on the occasion of the launch of the 1838 Reserve ICICI Bank Credit Card, featuring Krishen Khanna’s Bandwalla artwork, Aman Nath draws a connection with an earlier moment when The Times of India helped bring art into a new arena

An archival picture of the first printed edition of The Times of India from November 3, 1838. It was called The Bombay Times and Journal of Commerce then

When India was young and dreaming

When ₹10 lakh was a headline

Twenty-two lakh, doubled

1838 Reserve credit card: Culture, Travel Community & More

Access to culture, community and travel

1838 Reserve credit card: Culture, Travel Community & More





At the launch of 1838 Reserve ICICI Bank Credit Card, a card featuring Krishen Khanna’s Bandwalla artwork, I found myself thinking about another moment when The Times of India brought art into an unfamiliar space. This time, it was a pocket. Back in 1989, it was an auction room, where Indian society was beginning to discover that a painting could be both a thing of beauty and an investment.The name 1838 takes us back to the beginning of The Times of India. Over the years, its circulation grew beyond that of a city newspaper, and the newspaper became the largest-selling English daily in the world. Its pages followed political events, social tastes, sporting trends and spiritual musings, absorbing the contradictions of a country forever negotiating between its past and its future.In 1988-89, when The Times of India celebrated its sesquicentennial anniversary with nationwide celebrations, I was naturally involved. As a polyglot creative, I moved comfortably between the arts, advertising, design and music, though not gastronomy or gluttony. My simple eating habits were something I shared with the Ashok Jain family. Those celebrations were also when The Times of India showed its class to its contemporaries.At Vigyan Bhavan, the then Prime Minister, Rajiv Gandhi arrived amid the literati, glitterati and chatterati. There was a general euphoria in the hall. He made it roar with laughter when he began by saying he was delighted to be at the ‘sexy-centennial.. oops! The sesquicentennial celebrations’. His friend Mani Shankar Aiyar (former diplomat and politician) had written the speech!India was young, dreaming of shedding the burdens of servitude and underdevelopment so that it could fly. A pilot gave us hope, and the newspaper became the anarchic script in which India was old and young, wise and foolish, eastern and western. It absorbed medieval and modern dichotomies with such ease that evenFellini could not have fitted those anomalies into a single frame.Aroon Purie’s observation that all governments have an 18-month honeymoon began to play out. The newspaper, meanwhile, went from strength to strength.As part of those celebrations, The Times of India collaborated with Sotheby’s to conduct an international art auction in 1989. It was a pioneering step towards internationalising Indian art. Before the auction, an extensive campaign in The Economic Times introduced readers to the value of art. It explained how works that an artist could not sell in his lifetime could later become million-dollar investments. Seven advertisements that I had made explored this idea, including how an investment in art could yield more than one in land. People read them carefully. India read and registered.The auction was famously hosted aboard a ship (training ship Jawahar) in Mumbai. Stilettos and low necklines accompanied bidding paddles that were, in fact, table-tennis racquets of wealth. A new Indian society was announcing its arrival. That was when MF Husain first broke the ₹10 lakh mark, a milestone in the art world. A painting selling for more than a lakh was difficult to believe. It made headlines because art was not yet in that league.Today, when a Ravi Varma sells for more than ₹100 crore, it makes headlines. Back then, ₹10 lakh was the shocking figure. The Times of India was pioneering the thought that art was money, and it can take credit for recognising that possibility. Having eyes into the future is a large part of understanding art.On the day of the auction, I was having lunch with the The Times of India team at the Taj Mahal Hotel. Samir Jain told us that they had put in ₹22 lakh to buy the works. The artists wanted their works bought for the auction; they did not want to bear the risk themselves.“I really hope you recover the money,” he said to me. I assured him that he would. In fact, I said, he would get ₹44 lakh. Everybody laughed.After the auction, when the proceeds from all the paintings were totalled, the figure was an unbelievable ₹44 lakh.These sound like such small sums today. Yet they capture the scale of a moment when Indian art was entering a new world of recognition and value. Seeing Khanna’s work on the 1838 Reserve card brought that memory back: Another encounter between art and everyday life, with a newspaper’s long history running through it.With maestro Krishen Khanna’s iconic Bandwalla artwork on its metal body and a name that recalls the year The Times of India first went to print, the 1838 Reserve ICICI Bank Credit Card is a unique blend of art, heritage and luxury. Launched on Monday at an evening hosted by Samir Jain, Vice Chairman, BCCL, and Satyan Gajwani, Vice Chairman, Times Internet Ltd, it is a premium, invite-only credit card and the first in India on Visa Infinite Privilege – Visa’s highest tier.The 1838 Reserve ICICI Bank card opens doors to a world of culture, community, sport, travel and exceptional experiences, bringing together thoughtfully curated privileges from India and around the world. Cardholders enjoy membership of The Quorum for as long as they hold the card, joining a community of founders, investors, creators and cultural leaders.Journeys become more effortless with at-home visa biometrics, fast-track security and immigration, international airport transfers and zero forex markup. From stays at Lohono Platinum Villas to Accor Explorer membership, every privilege offers another way to explore the world with greater ease.
Article Summary: 1838 Reserve ICICI Bank Credit Card features Krishen Khanna’s Bandwalla artwork. Aman Nath draws a connection with an earlier moment when The Times of India helped bring art into a new arena. In 1989, Indian society was beginning to discover that a painting could be both a thing of beauty and an investment.

Article Title: A mother’s bone helped rebuild daughter’s damaged thigh five years back, hosp later cured more kids
Article Text: New Delhi: In 2021, a 16-year-old girl’s thigh bone, ravaged by a chronic infection, was reconstructed by Delhi doctors using a piece of bone taken from her mother’s lower leg. Five years later, the rebuilt bone continues to grow.The surgery also offered the doctors a new approach which they have used for curing other children who were advised amputation.Doctors said the challenge in these cases was the size of the defect. According to the surgeon treating the girl, the six children who underwent the procedure had bone gaps measuring around 12-13 cm. Three had bone cancer, two had chronic infections and one had a fracture that had failed to heal.When such a large section of a bone is lost, reconstruction becomes difficult. The child’s own bone may not be available in sufficient quantity, while conventional replacement options may not be suitable for every case. So, the team used the mother’s fibula -- the smaller of the two bones in the lower leg -- to bridge the gap and help rebuild the affected bone in the child.The first operation was performed in 2021. The surgeon said the team’s literature search at the time found only one reported case of maternal bone grafting in a child.It was for the forearm.The surgical team at Aakash Healthcare Super Speciality Hospital, Delhi, subsequently treated five more children using the approach.“When the first mother offered her bone, we had very little to guide us.... We asked ourselves whether it could work in the leg and decided the child deserved the chance,” said Dr Aashish Chaudhry, director and head of orthopaedics and robotic joint replacement., Aakash Healthcare.The later cases included children with bone cancers, some of whom had reportedly been advised to undergo amputation in their home countries. The second patient, a 14-year-old girl, underwent the procedure in 2022 after a chronic bone infection and a fracture in weakened bone left her thigh bone poorly healed.Four more children from Uzbekistan and Tajikistan have since undergone similar reconstructive surgery. Two boys -- aged five and 11 – both advised above-knee amputation in their home country -- travelled from Uzbekistan after reportedly being advised to undergo above-knee amputation in their home country.Their treatment involved removing the diseased bone and reconstructing the defect with a segment of the mother’s fibula, secured with plates where required.
Article Summary: In 2021, a 16-year-old girl’s thigh bone, ravaged by a chronic infection, was reconstructed by Delhi doctors using a piece of bone taken from her mother's lower leg. Five years later, the rebuilt bone continues to grow. The surgery offered the doctors a new approach which they have used for curing other children who were advised amputation.

Article Title: 29-year-old tennis player, hailing from Novak Djokovic's country, handed 24-year ban
Article Text:
Representational Photo (AP)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
