Stefan Milicevic has been banned from the sport until October 2050 after being charged with match-fixing and attempting to recruit players into an alleged corruption network. The International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) announced the suspension on Thursday, along with a $70,000 fine.Milicevic hails from Serbia, a country with a rich tennis tradition that has produced several world-class players, most notably Novak Djokovic The 29-year-old was accused of fixing six matches, five of which he played in, and attempting to manipulate the outcomes of six additional matches between 2022 and 2024.The ITIA also charged him with recruiting or trying to recruit several professional players into a network allegedly involved in match-fixing during that period.Milicevic, who mainly competed in lower-tier tournaments, achieved a career-best singles ranking of 1,338 in 2014. According to the ITIA, the alleged network led to other players fixing matches. However, the agency did not reveal the specific matches involved or name the other players suspected of taking part.The ITIA said Milicevic failed to cooperate with its investigation and did not respond to its findings, despite seven attempts to contact him.His lack of engagement was cited as a factor in determining the severity of the sanction.Under the terms of the ban, Milicevic is prohibited from competing in, coaching at or attending tournaments organised or sanctioned by the ATP, WTA, Grand Slams, World Tennis or any national tennis association.The suspension will keep him out of the sport until he turns 53.Milicevic's punishment comes after French tennis player Quentin Folliot received a 20-year ban in December following an investigation that identified him as a central figure in an alleged match-fixing network operating on behalf of a syndicate.Folliot, who reached a career-high singles ranking of 488 in 2022, denied allegations concerning 11 matches played between 2022 and 2024. However, following a hearing, 27 of the 30 charges against him were upheld, covering 10 of those matches.
Article Summary: Stefan Milicevic has been banned from the sport until October 2050. The 29-year- old was charged with match-fixing and attempting to recruit players into an alleged corruption network. The International Tennis Integrity Agency announced the suspension on Thursday, along with a $70,000 fine.

An ABVP victory procession in Bhubaneswar





Bhubaneswar: The student union polls spilled beyond campus walls, with chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi and former chief minister Naveen Patnaik on Friday trading barbs on social media as Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ) and BJD ’s student wing Biju Chhatra Janatal Dal (BCJD) battled for supremacy.Eight years after student union elections were last held in Odisha , campuses turned into vibrant political battlegrounds as the ABVP, the RSS student wing, and BCJD engaged in a fiercely contested, lavishly funded and closely watched electoral showdown. The contest on Thursday unfolded amid colourful campaigning, aggressive outreach and intense mobilisation of first-time voters, drawing attention well beyond college gates.While ABVP won the maximum number of campuses, BCJD emerged a close second and secured victories in key institutions, including Ravenshaw University in Cuttack and Rama Devi Women’s University in Bhubaneswar, among others.Reacting to the elections, Majhi alleged that the previous govt had kept student union polls suspended to serve its political interests, depriving students of their democratic voice. “Our government fulfilled its promise to the student community by successfully conducting the elections and restoring the spirit of democracy on campuses,” he said in a social media post.Congratulating the newly elected student representatives across colleges and universities, Majhi wrote, “I am confident that they will uphold the trust of their fellow students, discharge their responsibilities with sincerity and integrity, strengthen democratic values on campuses and contribute meaningfully towards building a Viksit Odisha.”Naveen, on the other hand, said the outcome reflected the dedication and unity of Odisha’s Gen Z, youth and student power, while accusing the BJP govt of attempting to influence the polls. “I commend all the members of BJD and BCJD who stood firmly against the BJP govt’s conspiracy to win the student union election through injustice and unfair means. Let us all unite to move forward in maintaining the academic environment of the college and shaping a bright future for the students,” he posted on X.Countering Naveen, BJD MLA Irasis Acharya said it was the former chief minister who had conspired to keep students away from the democratic process by suspending union elections since 2018. However, govt led by Majhi resumed the process. Acharya said student union elections help sensitise the younger generation about democracy and groom future leaders.With mainstream parties sharpening their focus on Gen Z and millennial voters ahead of the panchayat and urban local body elections scheduled for March-April next year, the student polls are being seen as a key political barometer. More than a fight for campus leadership, they offer an early glimpse into the mood of a new generation of voters and could serve as a crucial tee-off point for larger electoral contests in the months ahead.Political analysts said the enthusiasm shown by top political leaders during this year’s campus polls was aimed at signalling support among Gen Z voters at a time when youth-led protests against the establishment in Delhi and other parts of the country have attracted attention. “While the prolonged gap in student polls has added to the excitement, parties clearly want to showcase that youths are with them,” said Jayant Mohapatra, a retired political science professor.
Article Summary: Eight years after student union elections were last held in Odisha, campuses turned into vibrant political battlegrounds. ABVP, the RSS student wing, and BCJD engaged in a fiercely contested, lavishly funded and closely watched electoral showdown. Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi alleged that the previous govt had kept student union polls suspended to serve its political interests.

Article Title: An Indiana man sketched a backyard pool on a napkin after a 1.5-year installation wait; two years later it became a 60,000-gallon private water park now renting for $140 an hour
Article Text:
Pic credit: Swimply/ Mandy

He wanted a pool, but they asked him to wait

Pic credit: Swimply/ Mandy

Pic credit: Swimply/ Mandy

Two pools in two years

Pic credit: Swimply/ Mandy

Inside the private backyard water park

Pic credit: Swimply/ Mandy

You can rent it for $140 an hour

Pic credit: Swimply/ Mandy

Plenty of people dream about a backyard pool. Cory Johnson built a water park. On the east side of Lake Wawasee in Cromwell, his home shares its grounds with a 60,000-gallon private retreat that has waterfalls, a slide, a zip line and real palm tree trunks. Then he rents it out for $140 an hour!Walk in, and the first question is how anyone fitted a lagoon into a backyard. The second is obviously when you can book it!Like many others, Cory Johnson wanted a backyard pool where he could relax on the lounge chairs and enjoy his days. He initially set out to get a pool. A few years ago, he learned that the installation wait would stretch to about a year and a half, according to a report by inkfreenews. Rather than sitting around, he started sketching what he wanted on a napkin. That took him down memory lane.Ever since The Legend of Billie Jean came out, he had wanted a pool that he could jump into, or perhaps slide into straight from the house. "I watched the movie 'The Legend of Billie Jean' back in the '80s. (In) one of the scenes, a guy slides out of the window. He slides out of the window right into a pool. I said, 'I want to do that.I'm going to build that someday,'" he told Goshen News earlier.So, when he discovered that he would have to wait another year for the pool installation, he thought he would build it himself. "It can't be that hard," he told the outlet.The outdoor pool went up using blocks mortared together and reinforced with rebar. Johnson built the walls himself. Contractors poured the foundation, and Amish brothers finished much of the structure. The work took two years, including a six-month break in between. Both pools were finished in September 2023.The indoor pool took four days to fill! Cory Johnson's wife, Mandy, who was part of the project from the start, remembers checking the water line every morning. "Every morning, we'd wake up and come out here and see where the water line was. It was just neat every day to watch it fill up."The indoor/outdoor pool holds about 60,000 gallons of heated salt water, maintained at between 85 and 87 degrees year-round. Two pumps, two salt generators and oversized filters keep the water clean. Johnson still wants to cut back on chlorine, so he's thinking about adding a UV and ozone system.The indoor pool has a lagoon aesthetic. Fresh water rains down from a perforated pipe in a ceiling 20 to 30 feet up. A waterfall pours over giant rocks behind it. There is a zip line that sends guests flying towards them before they drop safely into the water.The custom slide is what catches people off guard. It ends higher above the water than most expect, so the ride is faster than they planned for. It sits on a 5-inch stainless steel pipe reinforced with concrete and rebar, then covered in stone so that it blends in. Mandy calls it a "beach vacation oasis".Cory Johnson's pool in Cromwell won Swimply's Choice Award for 2026 for its distinctive design, which recreates the look of a waterfall landscape and incorporates natural outdoor elements into the pool area.Today, the Johnsons rent it out for $140 an hour. On average, they get five to six bookings a day. They also provide snorkelling gear, pool toys and professional underwater scooters used by scuba divers.The couple never planned to rent the pool. They hadn't even heard of Swimply when they started building. Now they rarely use the pool themselves, except for cleaning and maintenance.Mandy says many first-time guests don't believe the pool is real until they see it! One guest, who usually booked hotels or visited attractions for their daughter's birthday, said the experience at Johnson's property was the best yet. "This place is amazing! Every year for my daughter's birthday, we usually get a hotel so her friends and family can celebrate and swim. We have gone to Kalahari Yogi Bear camp ground ect. My daughter said this was the best birthday ever!" the review on Swimply reads. Another agreed: "The best space for a party! My son and his friends had an absolute blast. The host was also so laid back and pleasant to talk to. 10/10 would rent again and would recommend!"The pool stays open all year, so the Johnsons decorate it for winter with a 14-foot Christmas tree. Mandy says the children who walk in see the tree and the pool together, and it's "just like a double win for them".Cory Johnson isn't done. He's already dreaming about a steam cave and a hot spring that runs hotter than normal. "That'll probably never happen, but you never know. We don't like little. Go big or go home," he told the outlet.
Article Summary: Cory Johnson wanted a backyard pool where he could relax on the lounge chairs and enjoy his days. The indoor/outdoor pool holds about 60,000 gallons of heated salt water, maintained at between 85 and 87 degrees year-round. The work took two years, including a six-month break in between.

Article Title: Hingoli man kills wife at in-laws’ farm, attacks mother-in-law; later ends life
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A dispute over a woman staying at her parental home ended in a double tragedy in Hingoli district on Wednesday evening. A man allegedly bludgeoned his wife to death, seriously injured his mother-in-law when she tried to intervene, and later died by suicide by hanging himself from a nearby tree.The deceased were identified as Deepali Paikrao and her husband Vishal Dongre, both in their mid-20s. Deepali’s mother, Kamalbai, sustained serious injuries and is undergoing treatment.According to police, both families are engaged in farming.Hingoli superintendent of police Shrenik Lodha said, “Deepali had married Vishal, a resident of Dhanora Jahangir village. However, she had returned to her parental home, in Kharwad village of Kalamnuri taluka, after Vishal allegedly began harassing her following their marriage.”She had been staying with her parents at their agricultural field for the past few days. Police said Vishal had repeatedly asked Deepali to return with him. On Wednesday evening, he went to her parents’ farm to convince her to come back. An argument broke out between the couple over her decision to stay with her parents.In a fit of rage, Vishal allegedly picked up a wooden plank from a cot and struck Deepali on the head. She died on the spot.When Kamalbai rushed to stop the assault, Vishal allegedly attacked her as well, leaving her severely injured.Some time later, Kamalbai’s husband and son arrived at the farm, found the victims and took them to hospital. They then alerted the police.During the subsequent search, police found Vishal hanging from a tree a few metres away from the scene of the crime.Based on Kamalbai’s complaint, Kalamnuri police on Thursday registered a murder case against Vishal. Senior officers visited the spot and carried out a panchanama.
Article Summary: A dispute over a woman staying at her parental home ended in a double tragedy in Hingoli district. A man allegedly bludgeoned his wife to death, seriously injured his mother-in-law when she tried to intervene, and later died by suicide by hanging himself from a nearby tree. The deceased were identified as Deepali Paikrao and her husband Vishal Dongre, both in their mid-20s.

Article Title: Satara forest department action against teak wood transportation
Article Text:
Satara Forest Department seizes teak wood worth Rs 2.5 lakh

Kolhapur

:





Forest officials in Satara have seized a tractor-trolley allegedly transporting teak wood illegally and registered a case against the driver under the Indian Forest Act, 1927.Acting on a tip-off, a forest team intercepted the vehicle on the Masur-Nigdi road and found teak wood being transported without a permit. The seized wood and vehicle are collectively valued at about Rs 2.5 lakh.“Our team set a trap near the canal, and a tractor was inspected. It contained teak wood being transported without a license. When interrogated, the tractor driver was unable to give any justification or provide documents,” said assistant conservator of forests Jayashree Jadhav.The tractor driver, Gorakh Shiratode, has been taken into custody. “The seized goods have been safely kept at Varade forest department office for security reasons,” Jadhav added.
Article Summary: Satara Forest Department seizes teak wood worth Rs 2.5 lakh. The seized wood and vehicle are collectively valued at about £2.5. The tractor driver, Gorakh Shiratode, has been taken into custody. The goods have been safely kept at Varade forest department office.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Mumbai-Goa highway crash: 30-year-old killed, 2 cousins injured after Honda City hits gate
Article Text:
30-year-old Akshay Kadam lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man driving his Honda City car was killed and his two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured after the driver lost control over the wheels on the Mangaon-Mahad stretch of Mumbai-Goa highway after crossing Mangaon railway station and veering off the road crashed into the iron gate of an industrial unit.The fatal accident occured on Monday around 3 am, when the three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon and were returning to their respective villages in Mahad taluka.The injured complainant stated in the FIR registered at Mangaon police station that the accused car driver and his cousin had consumed liquor before going for dinner.The deceased driver was identified as Akshay Arjun Kadam, a resident of Nandgaon, Mahad taluka. Those injured are Rohit Rajendra Dhadve (24), working as safety officer at Astriel Life Science Pvt Ltd in Mahad MIDC and his cousin Roshan Dilip Dhadve (24). Both residents of Kembhurli, Mahad taluka.Maruti Andhale, senior inspector of Mangaon said, "As the complainant Rohit Dhadve has stated in the FIR that the accused Akshay Kadam drove the car after consuming liquor along with his cousin Roshan, when they had meet near the bus stop, after which they went to Mangaon for dinner, the Motor Vehicle Act section for drunk driving will be invoked.However, as the accused car driver Akshay Kadam responsible for the car crash had died in the accident, a final closure 'Abated summary' report will be submitted before the Mangaon magistrate court. "As per the FIR by the complainant Rohit Dhadve, on Sept 28 around 1 am, when he was at home, his paternal cousin Roshan spoke to him over mobile, when Roshan's maternal cousin Akshay Kadam accompanying him told Rohit that he had come from Mumbai and asked him to meet near the bus stand at Kembhurli.When Rohit met them at the spot, Roshan and Akshay were consuming liquor inside Akshay's Honda City car. Thereafter, Akshay said, "Let's go to Mangaon to have food and the three of them went in the car with Akshay at the wheels."Roshan was sitting beside Akshay and Rohit on the rear seat. They reached Mangaon around 2 am, where they ate parathas at a road side food stall and took parcel of Khima Pav.Thereafter, they drove for 3 kms towards Indapur and took a U-turn to return to their villages in Mahad.After crossing 300 metres from Mangaon railway Station, Akshay lost control over the wheels and yanking off the road on the right side, he crashed into the iron gate of Sundha Steel Traders industrial unit.Rohit sustained injuries below his left eye, left hand and left knee. Akshay got stuck between the driver's seat and the door. Roshan's left leg was injured.Hearing the loud noice of the car crash, the locals gathered, removed the three injured out of the car and summoned 108 ambulance in which they were rushed to Mangaon sub-district hospital, where Akshay was declared brought dead on arrival.
Article Summary: Akshay Arjun Kadam, 30, lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle on the Mumbai-Goa highway. His two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured. The three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon.

Article Title: Nagpur’s NCC cadets help Maha excel at Sainik Camp

Nagpur’s NCC Air Wing cadets help Maharashtra secure top honours at AIVSC 2026, showcasing excellence in aviation and aeromodelling

Article Title: Kovai Heroes: This woman has helped scores of birds get a second chance in sky
Article Text:
A resident of Sivananda Colony with a doctorate in environmental science, Vinny turned a childhood passion for birdwatching into a lifelong defence of avian life. (Photo by J Jackson)

Kovai Heroes is a city-wide recognition initiative by The Times of India, presented by Infinium developers to identify, celebrate and honour individuals who are making a positive impact in Coimbatore through their work, service, innovation, leadership or acts of kindness. Education Partner: SSVM Institutions. Associate Partner: Lakshmi Ceramics.





COIMBATORE: Inside a quiet recovery enclosure, a rescued Alexandrine parakeet stretches its wings, testing the flight muscles that have withered after years of captivity. A few cages away, an injured peafowl rests under veterinary observation, recovering from electrical burns sustained on high voltage wires. At the centre of this relentless healing mission is Vinny R Peter, 42, a wetland ecologist whose life’s work revolves around giving birds a second chance in the sky.A resident of Sivananda Colony with a doctorate in environmental science, Vinny turned a childhood passion for birdwatching into a lifelong defence of avian life. As director of community education for the NGO Animal Rescuers, she operates on the frontlines of urban wildlife conservation, bridging community distress calls with rapid medical intervention in partnership with the Tamil Nadu forest department.For Vinny, urban skies present a labyrinth of hazards caused by human activities -- lethal manja threads, concrete sprawl and exposed electrical transformers.Vinny says some of the deepest wounds she has seen stem from illegal confinement. “Parakeets are born to fly, not to mimic human names,” she says.“Birds possess the fundamental right to flight. Alexandrine parakeets naturally fly up to 40 kilometres a day.We clip their wings and tail feathers, and keep them confined in tiny iron cages for years,” she says.Her team frequently rehabilitates parakeets confiscated from roadside fortune-tellers -- often with severely damaged beaks -- as well as domestic pets trapped in human habits. One rescued bird could only mimic the roar of a motorcycle exhaust; another called out the name “Meenu” repeatedly. Through sustained public awareness drives, several residents have voluntarily surrendered caged birds after realizing that possessing protected wild species violates wildlife laws.Operating out of the Avian Recuperation Centre in the District Forest Officer complex on the Mettupalayam Road, Vinny and her volunteer network coordinate care with the forest department’s frontline staffers and specialized veterinarians. Equipped with in-house diagnostic tools like X-ray units, the facility handles complex fractures, open trauma, dehydration in migratory birds and orphaned chicks. Over the past 15 years, the organization has rescued and sheltered more than 13,000 native and migratory birds, even providing critical care to rare visitors like the endangered Egyptian vulture.However, treatment is only the halfway mark. Every bird is rehabilitated in specialized flight enclosures designed to rebuild flight stamina before being released back into native canopies.Beyond immediate medical rescue, Vinny actively focuses on shaping future mindsets. Through school tours at the recuperation centre and urban outreach campaigns, she educates young students on urban biodiversity, bird-friendly landscaping and the simple act of setting out water bowls during summer. By teaching the next generation to view wild birds not as pets to possess but as vital architects of the ecosystem, Vinny ensures that Coimbatore’s skies remain alive with full-throated songs of happy birds.
Article Summary: Vinny R Peter is a wetland ecologist whose life’s work revolves around giving birds a second chance in the sky. As director of community education for the NGO Animal Rescuers, she operates on the frontlines of urban wildlife conservation. Over the past 15 years, she has rescued and sheltered more than 13,000 native and migratory birds.

Article Title: Kovai Heros: Meet ‘Eera Nenjam’ Mahendiran, who has rescued over 1,000 destitute people from Coimbatore streets
Article Text:
P Mahendiran with elderly women residing in his shelter

Kovai Heroes

is a city-wide recognition initiative by The Times of India, presented by Infinium developers to identify, celebrate and honour individuals who are making a positive impact in Coimbatore through their work, service, innovation, leadership or acts of kindness. Education Partner: SSVM Institutions. Associate Partner: Lakshmi Ceramics





COIMBATORE: In 1992, young P Mahendiran, his mother and his elder sister were going to temple. Mahendiran’s sister, who was suffering from mental health issues, fell into a roadside sewage drain. As bystanders kept their distance, an anonymous autorickshaw driver entered the drain to rescue her. That single act of empathy left a permanent mark on Mahendiran, who was 16 years then. Years later, in 2005, the incident motivated Mahendiran to become a Good Samaritan in the streets of Coimbatore.By 2009, Mahendiran, a resident of Gandhipuram, had single-handedly rescued 16 people and placed them in private shelters. That year marked a pivotal shift when he reunited a man named Ashokan with his family. Ashokan had been missing for 15 years, and his family had already performed his last rites believing he was dead. This emotional reunion taught Mahendiran that rescuing individuals was merely the first step; returning them to their loved ones was the real goal.Encouraged by his friends, Mahendiran launched the Eera Nenjam Trust in 2012.Over the past two decades, he has rescued more than 1,000 people from the streets and successfully reunited around 400 with their families across the country and beyond.“Eera Nenjam” Mahendiran, as he is now known, is often contacted by passersby when they find a destitute person lying on roadsides -- often unwashed, with matted hair, and ignored by the public. Armed with a bucket, shaving tools, and immense patience, he steps in where even medical workers sometimes hesitate."People with mental health issues need to be handled with great care. Our approach must be filled with love and concern. We have to patiently go near them, cut their hair, bathe them, give them clean clothes and then take them to a shelter or hospital," he says. For 50-year-old Mahendiran, this work goes far beyond basic rescue operations; it is about restoring lost dignity and guiding the forgotten back home.The support from a hospital in Bengaluru helped him provide treatment to homeless people who needed urgent medical attention. But his responsibility does not end with treatment."When a homeless person dies after treatment fails, I cannot leave the body unattended. I make sure the person is given a respectful burial," he notes. Aided by a crematorium worker named Vairamani, he ensures dignity in death.He manages the financial strain without actively soliciting funds, relying on voluntary contributions from friends. "Income is limited, but the expenses are high. We use whatever we have and continue the work. Service should never stop because of money," he says.The impact of Eera Nenjam also extends beyond street rescues. For eight years, elderly women residing in his shelter have prepared breakfast for nearly 300 students at a govt school in RS Puram. Predating the Tamil Nadu govt’s breakfast scheme, this initiative gave abandoned mothers a renewed sense of purpose.Mahendiran balances his small business and family life with his social work. He notes a recent decline in rescue calls, attributing it to increased public awareness and better shelter infrastructure. Yet, his core motivation remains unchanged. "When we rescue a person from the roadside, help them recover, find their family and reunite them with their loved ones, the happiness in their eyes is the biggest blessing," he says.
Article Summary: P Mahendiran has rescued more than 1,000 people from the streets of Coimbatore. He has also successfully reunited around 400 with their families across the country. For eight years, elderly women residing in his shelter have prepared breakfast for nearly 300 students at a govt school.

Article Title: Female elephant dies despite treatment in ATR
Article Text:
Preliminary examination by the veterinary team indicated a stomach ulcer and infections in its internal organs

Coimbatore:





A female elephant which was found in a critical condition in a reserve forest behind the Navamalai electricity board employees’ quarters in the Pollachi forest range earlier in the day, died on Monday night despite more than 10 hours of intensive treatment by forest department personnel and a veterinary team.Forest department officials were alerted about the ailing elephant, which was found in the reserve forest under the Anamalai Tiger Reserve. A team from Pollachi forest range reached the spot around noon. After a two-hour long effort, forest staff drove away the herd and levelled the ground to facilitate treatment. The team then administered intravenous fluids and injections to improve the elephant’s condition and alleviate its pain. Its body temperature and other vital parameters were monitored. However, it died around 10pm on Monday without responding to treatment.A postmortem was subsequently conducted on Tuesday. “The elephant was weak, possibly because of its age, which may have affected its immunity. We noticed internal bleeding, which could explain why it fell ill and remained lying down without responding to treatment,” a forest department official said.Preliminary examination by the veterinary team indicated a stomach ulcer and infections in its internal organs. However, officials said further analysis was required to establish the exact cause of death and determine what led to the infections.The carcass was left in the forest to be consumed by scavengers and other wildlife. A total of 28 forest department personnel, along with veterinarians, were involved in the treatment and postmortem procedures.
Article Summary: A female elephant was found in a critical condition in a reserve forest in Coimbatore. It died on Monday night despite more than 10 hours of intensive treatment by forest department personnel and a veterinary team. A postmortem was subsequently conducted on Tuesday. Preliminary examination by the veterinary team indicated a stomach ulcer and infections in its internal organs.
